correctness.rationale: The kernel is strictly positive with exact prescribed marginals and a symmetric normalized eigenmode s. Differentiating the nonlinear row/column scalings yields \(DS(0)=s^2\) on the gauge-free direction. Differentiating the source-specified coupled update gives the displayed exact trace and determinant; direct rational arithmetic checks confirm the Schur-stability identities. The critical parameter solves an increasing quadratic, has a repeated positive eigenvalue, lies in the allowed range, and is the unique global spectral-radius minimum by determinant lower bounds below it and a negative characteristic-polynomial evaluation above it. The exact threshold is obtained by the algebraic sign identity for G_s(s^{-1}-1). The embedded finite-difference tests check the actual nonlinear map and supplement, not replace, the analytic universal proof. This establishes only local spectral factors, not global rates or a pure critical \(O(q^k)\) norm inequality.

value.rationale: An actual 2026 acceleration for regularized optimal transport may lose to its original Sinkhorn iteration in the locally strongly mixed regime. The proved sharp \(s^2=1/4\) boundary and explicit unique optimal allowed tuning identify precisely when fixed-parameter acceleration helps or hurts in the natural minimal transport instance. This parameter-selection and algorithm-comparison fact is not the generic statement that acceleration sometimes slows down: it classifies the full positive balanced two-atom family, includes a constructive realizable kernel for every spectral value, and proves local stability. It is useful as a diagnostic and benchmark even though no higher-dimensional or global theorem is claimed.
